The informal March incident estimate was approximately 20 affected customers, as noted by Chloe Dupont and agreed by Raj Patel in the engineering standup (NL-022-S03). However, the final official impact, confirmed after the complete postmortem audit of database transaction logs, was exactly 17 customer workspaces (NL-022-S03). The postmortem (NL-013-S09) explicitly establishes the postmortem database audit as the sole authority for customer-impact metrics, thereby superseding the informal engineering guess of ~20 made before audits were complete.

The corrective work that addresses recurrence includes: (1) enforcing a retry cap with exponential backoff and randomized jitter (max 5 retries) for background worker jobs, completed March 15, 2026 (NL-013-S07); (2) mandating multi-stage, lock-free schema migrations for tables larger than 100,000 rows, completed March 16, 2026 (NL-013-S07); (3) implementing granular Redis queue monitoring alerts (target June 2026) (NL-013-S07); (4) conducting ingestion load testing under connection-starvation scenarios (target July 2026) (NL-013-S07); and (5) separating database connection pools for write-heavy background tasks and read-heavy user query interfaces (target August 2026) (NL-013-S07). Additionally, the SRE runbook's database recovery section has been revised and quarterly simulated disaster recovery drills are planned to validate response procedures, with a target RTO of less than 30 minutes (NL-013-S09).
